text: The city and its power utility sign exclusive negotiating and confidentiality agreements with Energy Delivery Solutions.
source: Reso. 19-13667 and the Pittsburg Technology Park development agreement (2019), p. 1 (agreements dated Aug. 1, 2017); EDS confidentiality agreement (2017), p. 1

text: The city closes the money-losing municipal golf course.
source: Reso. 19-13667 (2019), p. 1; Draft Program EIR (July 2024), p. 3.4-3 (closed March 1, 2018)

text: The City Council directs staff to explore economic development on part of the former golf course.
The city gives Energy Delivery Solutions an option to buy about 100 acres.
source: Reso. 19-13667 (2019), p. 1 (June 5, 2018, option on about 101.7 acres)

text: The council approves a deal for a technology park with data centers, powered by the city’s utility at “rates below those of competing energy providers.” The city also agrees to help lift a federal “public use” deed restriction on some parcels.
source: Reso. 19-13667 and the development agreement (2019), p. 2, p. 6 and §5.8

text: AVAIO’s Pittsburg Data Hub LLC takes over Energy Delivery Solutions’ rights.
source: Memorandum of option agreement (Dec. 2025), p. 1 (Novation and Amendment Agreement, April 11, 2022)

text: The city sells about 102 acres, including the deed-restricted parcels, to an AVAIO Digital Partners I subsidiary for $16.8 million and lends it the full price. The loan requires the company to seek a PG&E grid connection within a year.
source: Reso. 22-14126 (2022), pp. 1-2 and 6; Fulfillment of obligation letter (July 10, 2023), p. 1

text: The city’s utility files the PG&E grid-connection application on the company’s behalf.
source: Fulfillment of obligation letter (July 10, 2023), p. 1

text: AVAIO’s engineer tells Delta Diablo, the wastewater agency, that the land north of the canal “will be a data center.”
source: Delta Diablo–Kimley-Horn emails, p. 4 (Ryan Bernal, Feb. 7, 2024)

text: The city sends out its first formal environmental notice for the “Pittsburg Technology Park Specific Plan.” Its third page says Phase 1 would include “a data center and corresponding substation.”
source: Notice of Preparation (Feb. 28, 2024), p. 3; Draft Program EIR (July 2024), p. 1.0-4

text: A state filing lists Pittsburg Data Hub as the applicant for the technology park plan.
source: CEQAnet, SCH No. 2024030184 (notice received March 6, 2024; Pittsburg Data Hub LLC listed as project applicant)

text: The draft environmental report describes the Pittsburg Data Hub in detail, including its 37 generators.
source: Draft Program EIR (July 2024), p. ES-2 and p. 2.0-1

text: The City Council unanimously approves the plan, the environmental report and a map dividing the land into parcels.
source: Reso. 24-14560 (Nov. 4, 2024); settlement agreement, Exhibit 2 recitals

text: The Center for Biological Diversity sues the city over the environmental review.
source: Settlement agreement, PDF p. 3 (petition filed Dec. 2, 2024)

text: AVAIO announces “Perseus,” an $800 million, 92-megawatt project powered through a partnership with the city’s utility.
source: AVAIO press release, Dec. 3, 2024

text: City Attorney Donna Mooney asks the state Fair Political Practices Commission whether Dionne Adams, a PG&E employee and vice chair of the city utility’s board, can vote on its agreement with PG&E.
source: FPPC advice request emails, pp. 6-7 (request received Nov. 13, 2025)

text: The California Energy Commission exempts the generator yard from state licensing.
source: CEC staff responses to Scot Scoop, p. 1

text: Mooney writes to the FPPC: “For business reasons, staff here is eager to receive advice from the FPPC.”
source: FPPC advice request emails, p. 4 (Mooney, Dec. 10, 2025)

text: The zoning administrator approves the design. Mooney signs a joint request with the Center to pause its lawsuit.
source: Notice of Determination, SCH No. 2025100607, p. 1 (design review approved Dec. 11, 2025); settlement agreement, PDF p. 4

text: With Adams recused, the council votes 4-0 to let City Manager Darin Gale rewrite the loan, cutting the debt to $10.5 million.
The Center files the settlement in court. It agrees not to oppose Phase 1.
source: Settlement agreement, PDF pp. 6, 22-23 and 45

text: The city files its final notice.
source: Notice of Determination, SCH No. 2025100607, p. 1 (filed Feb. 17, 2026)

text: The FPPC rules that Adams cannot take part in the PG&E agreement “in any manner.”
source: FPPC advice letter A-25-154 (Feb. 27, 2026), pp. 1-2

text: If the usual 30-day window to sue over the approval applied, it passes.
source: Settlement agreement, PDF p. 11, §1.2.4 (30-day challenge period after a notice of determination)

text: Resident Amhari Perkins learns of the data center from a council member’s Facebook post and starts a petition.
source: Interview with Amhari Perkins, transcript p. 21

text: The council votes 4-0 to draft a 45-day emergency moratorium on new data centers, including AVAIO’s Phases 2 and 3.
source: City of Pittsburg news release

text: The council adopts the moratorium unanimously, effective immediately. Phase 1 is exempt.
source: City of Pittsburg news release; Contra Costa News, Oct. 27, 2026
